reason: Phagocytes are shown clearing debris near the cut, a useful first part of wound repair.
expectation: The phagocytes will help clear debris from the wound.

effect: The wound is cleared of debris, so I can turn to supporting tissue repair.
reaction: The result matched the picture and was straightforward.
reason: Repair signals are shown acting on the nearby vessel, suggesting they can help establish a blood supply for repair.
expectation: The signals will stimulate the nearby capillary to grow toward the wound.

effect: The signals produced a connected capillary sprout that can support the wound.
reaction: The vessel growing from an existing capillary makes the repair process easier to picture.
reason: Fibroblasts need raw materials to build supporting tissue, and the matrix nutrients supply them.
expectation: The fibroblasts will use the nutrients to make supporting wound matrix.

effect: The fibroblasts made new connective tissue, which can help support the damaged skin.
reaction: The collagen fibres make the supporting role clear.
reason: The new connective tissue appears ready to fill and support the cleaned wound.
expectation: The connective tissue will be added to the wound.

effect: The wound needed the capillary sprout first; the healing skin now has separate surface and support slots.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the required order, which I had not anticipated.
reason: The new connective tissue supplies the supporting dermis indicated by the empty support slot.
expectation: The connective tissue will fill the support slot.

effect: The connective tissue filled the support slot, leaving the surface to close.
reaction: The reminder that young tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin adds useful context.
reason: The epidermal edge cells need nutrients to grow and close the surface.
expectation: The cells will use the nutrients to form new surface tissue.

effect: The edge cells formed a new surface that can fill the remaining wound slot.
reaction: The sheet extending across the gap makes closure easy to picture.
reason: The new surface matches the empty surface slot in the healing skin.
expectation: The new surface will fill the slot and close the wound.

effect: The new surface closed the wound and completed the first goal; the temporary clot still needs clearing.
reaction: The distinction between surface closure and deeper tissue gaining strength is useful.
reason: Clot-clearing enzymes are described as breaking down fibrin, so they should address the remaining goal.
expectation: The enzymes will clear the temporary fibrin clot.

effect: The enzymes cleared most of the temporary fibrin, completing the repair goals; the scar continues to mature.
reaction: The distinction between removing the clot and continuing tissue repair was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the connective tissue was worthwhile because it showed how collagen supports the wound beneath the surface and explained that young tissue is still weaker than uninjured skin.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the connective tissue and the new surface felt somewhat repetitive: both involved combining cells with nutrients before adding the result to the body.

surprise.text: I expected to add connective tissue directly to the cleaned wound, but the body first combined with the capillary sprout. The feedback revealed the required order.

arbitrary.text: The requirement to add the capillary sprout before the connective tissue felt somewhat arbitrary; the chapter says repair jobs overlap, but did not explain why that order was necessary.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter. The wound sequence connected familiar events to cells, blood vessels and tissue, although I would hope for more varied decisions.
